rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> factorial randomized block field experiment at Wadi El-Tor, South Sinai, winter 2021, three replicates, two N rates x four drip fertigation schedules plus regular-irrigation control. Q2: Results 'Potato Yield and Yield Components' and Table 4 <U+2013> drip fertigation schedules increased tuber yield by 25.32% (N1) and 36.47% (N2) over regular irrigation; Table 4 gives tuber yields 23.14/28.56 t/ha for control vs 25.29<U+2013>42.76 t/ha for fertigation schedules. Q4: Table 5 and Fig. 2 <U+2013> total N uptake, N recovery and NUE measured for each treatment, tuber yield highly correlated with N uptake (R2 0.98 and 0.96); Fig. 3 and 'Nitrogen Movement in Soil' <U+2013> soil NO3-N at 0<U+2013>20 and 20<U+2013>40 cm measured, showing fertigation keeps nitrate in root zone while regular irrigation moves it deeper; LAI also measured (Table 4). Q7: Discussion 'Nitrogen Uptake, Recovery, and NUE' <U+2013> authors state drip irrigation can give full play to its advantages only under proper time and rate of N application; Conclusion <U+2013> stage-wise scheduling matched to growth curve is presented as the condition for the yield benefit, and nutrients must not be subject to leaching in sandy soil.
rows.notes: Single site, single season, single sandy soil, one potato cultivar; no triangulation (yield measured by one field method). The 'regular irrigation' control also differs in fertilizer application method (soil-applied N), so the drip vs regular comparison confounds irrigation method with fertigation; the passage is nonetheless a faithful restatement of the study's own result. Q7 has some doubt: the 'proper time and rate' condition is phrased as a requirement but partly echoes Li et al. 2021. Q8: no explicit limitations of the result are stated; the conclusion only notes that parameters need optimizing for other soils/crops. Q9: only LSD letter groupings and an ANOVA CV% (2.61%) are given; no SD, SE, CI or range for the yield means.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a one-season field trial on sandy soil in South Sinai, Egypt.
